When the previous revision's ApplicationStop script is broken, redeploy with the option to ignore ApplicationStop failures.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Longer timeout in the new appspec: the old script runs.
• Recreate the group: unnecessary.
• AllAtOnce: still runs the failing hook.

Key takeaway: broken old stop scripts → ignore ApplicationStop failures.

stem: Security requires that any security group allowing inbound SSH from 0.0.0.0/0 is fixed automatically within minutes in all accounts. Which solution meets this requirement?

choices.text: An SCP denying ec2:AuthorizeSecurityGroupIngress in all accounts.
The restricted-ssh Config rule with SSM auto-remediation, org-wide.
Amazon Inspector network reachability findings reviewed weekly.
A Trusted Advisor check with email notifications to the team.

explanation:
Why this is correct:
The restricted-ssh Config rule deployed org-wide with SSM auto-remediation fixes open SSH within minutes.

Why the other options are wrong:
• SCP denying all ingress changes: blocks legitimate use.
• Weekly Inspector review: slow.
• Trusted Advisor email: manual.

Key takeaway: auto-fix open SSH → Config + remediation.

stem: A company wants GuardDuty enabled in every account and Region of its organization, including accounts created in the future, with findings visible centrally in the security account. Which configuration fits BEST?

choices.text: A GuardDuty delegated administrator per Region with auto-enable.
Use CloudTrail Lake queries instead of GuardDuty.
Enable GuardDuty only in the management account.

stem: A buildspec currently contains a plaintext third-party API token in an environment variable. Security wants the token removed from source control and rotated centrally. What should the team do?

choices.text: Move the token into a README file in a private repository.
Secrets Manager, referenced in the buildspec env section.
Base64-encode the token in the buildspec.
Pass the token as a plaintext environment variable in the console.

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Storing the token in Secrets Manager and referencing it in the buildspec env secrets-manager section keeps it out of code and logs.

Why the other options are wrong:
• README: exposed.
• Base64: not encryption.
• Plaintext console variable: exposed.

Key takeaway: build secrets → Secrets Manager references.

stem: Over three years, many roles accumulated broad permissions. The security team wants to identify roles, access keys, and permissions that have not been used recently across the organization, so they can be removed. Which feature fits BEST?

choices.text: IAM Access Analyzer unused access analyzer.
AWS Config resource inventory.
IAM Access Analyzer external access analyzer.
IAM credential report only for the management account.

explanation:
Why this is correct:
IAM Access Analyzer's unused access analyzer finds unused roles, access keys, passwords, and permissions across the organization.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Config inventory: no usage data.
• External access analyzer: public/cross-account access.
• Credential report: one account and limited.

Key takeaway: find unused access → unused access analyzer.

stem: Developers need to create IAM roles for their own Lambda functions without platform team involvement, but must never create a role with more privileges than a defined set. Which approach enables this safely?

choices.text: Allow CreateRole only with a required permissions boundary.
Have developers share one administrator role for role creation.
Use an SCP that denies iam:CreateRole in all accounts.
Give developers iam:* permissions and review roles monthly.

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Allowing iam:CreateRole only when a specific permissions boundary is attached lets developers create roles that can't exceed the boundary.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Shared admin role: over-privileged.
• Deny CreateRole: blocks self-service.
• iam:* with monthly review: risky.

Key takeaway: safe delegated role creation → permissions boundaries.
